tax/turn beats: '$16.66B to the tax office' and 'only about $53.34B is left to give' ignore that a cash gift to a public charity is deductible (up to 60% of AGI, IRC 170(b)(1)(G), permanent since the 2025 tax act); giving the proceeds the same year would cut the 20% part of the bill a lot (only the 3.8% NIIT stays), so the tax loss and 'almost half would vanish' are overstated. Fix: say the tax is 'before any charity deduction' and soften the turn/hook, or reframe the tax as the cost of selling vs. giving shares (where the difference is real: no capital-gains tax at all on donated long-held shares).

payoff beat: 'hand the shares straight to a charity, which skips the sale and his tax bill' implies giving shares also avoids the 30% price slide; the charity still has to sell to spend the money and a $100B block hits the same thin buyer pool. Only the capital-gains tax is truly skipped. Fix: 'which skips his capital-gains tax' (optionally: 'and lets the charity sell slowly').
